episodes.204384: Hot and humid conditions beneath adequate wind shear from a passing weak upper wave combined with lift from a outflow boundary to initiate scattered strong thunderstorms on the afternoon of the 16th, with embedded severe cells impacted Fountain County and Hancock County.  Later in the evening, more organized strong to severe storms produced damage from eastern Madison County into northern portions of the Indianapolis Metro;  and then very early on the 17th, down to south-central Indiana, with one person injured while camping in Monroe County.  A total of 19,927 power outages occurred in central Indiana, including 7,468 in Hamilton County and 6,473 in Marion County.
episodes.204393: A series of weak, mainly convectively induced disturbances, resulted in the development of thunderstorms during the evening hours. Plenty of CAPE existed, but overall shear was weak, limiting organization.
episodes.204423: Scattered thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours of August 16, 2025. While these thunderstorms were generally non-severe, one thunderstorm did produce a brief 58 mph wind gust at the Crossville Airport.
episodes.204454: Most gusty outflow winds were throughout northern Utah.
episodes.204456: Showers caused strong winds for portions of I-15.
episodes.204577: Hot weather resulted in daily episodes of clusters of storms with damaging winds, isolated hail, and some areas of flash flooding from August 12 through August 18th.  The most widespread activity occurred August 15th, and 18th, when several lines of storms moved through the area.
episodes.204689: Scattered thunderstorms developed along an outflow boundary and tracked through central and east-central Wisconsin during the late morning hours on Saturday (8/16).  The strongest storms produced damaging winds across east-central Wisconsin.
episodes.204710: Diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms from the late evening hours of August 15, 2025 continued into the early morning hours of August 16th across eastern Pennsylvania. A non-severe thunderstorm drifted northward into Schuylkill County, producing efficient rainfall in a favorable moist environment, with gauge reports indicating between 3 and 6 inches of rainfall in a two-to-three hour timeframe. Flash flooding was observed in portions of Washington Township, with flooded roadways and basements. Diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms once again cropped up during the afternoon and evening hours of August 16, 2025 with locally heavy rainfall in Franklin County allowing for flooded roadways along the East Branch of Antietam Creek.
episodes.205071: Upper ridging in place to the west of the area, over the central US. A MCS developed east of the ridge axis and moved through the Deep South. Deep layer moisture in place and convergence from colliding outflow boundaries led to heavy rain. This caused urban flash flooding during the night of August 15th into the 16th.
episodes.205087: Thunderstorms developed in a highly unstable environment along a lingering boundary from a MCS that moved through the night before. Weak flow led to slow moving storms, propagating slowly along an outflow boundary. With precipitable water exceeding 2 inches and high soil moisture, this led to flash flooding near the Savannah River.
episodes.205174: Scattered thunderstorms resulted in a couple of measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.205381: Several storms/super cells moved across the northern Panhandle producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.205636: Isolated thunderstorms underneath a suppressive ridge occurred during the PM hours. One storm produced severe straight line wind damage in Morgan County, Tennessee.
episodes.205736: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed over Livingston and Washtenaw Counties.
episodes.205770: During the afternoon and evening of the 16th, a series of severe thunderstorms produced widespread damaging winds and instances of severe hail around the western and northwestern Chicago metro area.
episodes.205896: High moisture content and slow storm motion caused localized, flooding rainfall across Marion County where sea breeze storm mergers occurred in the evening.
episodes.205913: Periods locally heavy rainfall and flooding impacted northeast Florida during the afternoon and evening as a surface front across the area interacted with the sea breezes over a diurnally unstable and moist airmass. There was a Marginal Risk of flooding rainfall from the Weather Prediction Center. Precipitable water was 2-2.2 inches with storm motion less than 5 knots.
episodes.205914: Periods locally heavy rainfall and flooding impacted southeast Georgia during the morning and afternoon as a surface front across the area interacted with the sea breezes over a diurnally unstable and moist airmass. There was a Marginal Risk of flooding rainfall from the Weather Prediction Center. Precipitable water was 2-2.2 inches with storm motion less than 5 knots.
episodes.206493: Rounds of strong to severe storms throughout the day on August 16th resulted in instances of large hail, damaging winds and flash flooding in western Wisconsin. Hail with these storms reached up to golf ball sized near New Lisbon along with instances of tree damage. Later into the evening, additional storms moved through Grant County and produced heavy rainfall leading to flash flooding in Lancaster along with some quarter sized hail.
episodes.206514: Isolated thunderstorms tracked into the northeastern Nebraska Panhandle during the early evening hours of August 15th. This activity became severe with wind gusts up to 60 MPH reported north of Hay Springs. Later in the evening, thunderstorm wind gusts, estimated at 80 MPH destroyed an outbuilding and uprooted trees north of Ellsworth.
episodes.206515: During the overnight hours on August 16th, a lone severe thunderstorm moved through Winneshiek County and produced quarter sized hail in Calmar.
episodes.206517: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the Pine Ridge of northern Sheridan County during the early evening hours of August 16th. Hail up to quarter size was reported north of Hay Springs.
episodes.206529: Scattered thunderstorms formed along an outflow boundary along the I-74 corridor during the late afternoon and evening of August 16th.  One of the cells produced a brief EF-U tornado northeast of Homer in far western Vermilion County.  Other storms dropped hail as large as quarters and caused minor wind damage.
episodes.206560: The combination of an upper-level trough situated across the west coast and the subtropical high pressure situated over the Central Plains resulted in a south to southwest flow across the region. The combination of 500 mb temperatures near -8C and PWATs ranging between 1.3-1.5 inches resulted in MLCAPE values in excess of 1000 J/KG. A Mesoscale Convective Complex moving northward from Mexico triggered showers and thunderstorms across portions of western Pinal and southwestern Maricopa Counties with more isolated activity across northern La Paz County during the mid and late afternoon hours.
episodes.206743: An overnight mesoscale convective system developed over eastern South Dakota and southwest Minnesota early Saturday morning on August 16th. The bowing system grew in scale as it overspread portions of western and central Minnesota. There were several measured wind gusts over 60 mph, and even a couple over 70 mph in eastern Yellow Medicine county. Most of the wind damage reports of downed trees and powerlines were delayed and estimated using radar given that the storms moved through early in the morning.
episodes.206744: Several individual rounds of thunderstorms impacted southern Minnesota from Friday, August 16th through Sunday, August 18th. Heavy rain amounts on the order of 5-10 inches fell over the course of 72 hours, most of which fell from late Saturday into early Sunday, leading to several cases of flooded roadways and damaged buildings. The highest amounts and most widespread impacts were across Waseca County.
episodes.206795: Thunderstorms moving across northeast South Dakota during the early morning hours produced strong winds and wind damage, heavy rainfall, and a brief tornado. A peak wind gust of 80 mph was recorded at the South Dakota Department of Transportation (SDDOT) mesonet station 4 miles west southwest of Stone Bridge, while the SDDOT mesonet station near Turnerville recorded a peak wind gust of 77 mph. Winds were so strong in and around Watertown that the Codington County Emergency Manager reported an innumerable number of trees had fallen across town.
episodes.206858: A weak wave lifting out of the central Rockies aided in the initiation of a forward propagating Mesoscale Convective System from the lee of the Black Hills southward into the Nebraska Panhandle. With abundant MUCAPE up to nearly 4000 J/kg and DCAPE up to 1500 J/kg, but deep-layer shear only around 20-25 knots, storms retained a somewhat outflow dominant character while on an east-northeast trek. Winds were generally from 60 to 80 mph with significant damage to trees and a few structures along the track of the system north of Interstate 90 into southwest Minnesota. Around 600 customers were without power across Jerauld, Sanborn and Kingsbury Counties.
episodes.206865: An upper level disturbance and nearby stationary front led to multiple rounds of severe thunderstorms across southern WI. Large hail and damaging straight line winds led to trees down and some structural damage.
episodes.206869: A weak wave lifting out of the central Rockies aided in initiation of a forward propagating Mesoscale Convective system from the lee of the Black Hills southward into the Nebraska Panhandle. With abundant MUCAPE up to nearly 4000 J/kg and DCAPE up to 1500 J/kg, but deep-layer shear only around 20-25 knots, storms retained a somewhat outflow dominant character while on an east-northeast trek. Winds were generally from 60 to 80 mph with significant damage to trees and a few structures along the track of the system north of Interstate 90 into southwest Minnesota.
episodes.206911: A weak cold front encountering deep moisture led to slow moving thunderstorms capable of producing heavy rainfall across Southeast South Carolina.
episodes.207018: Strong thunderstorms occurred on the afternoon and evening of August 15th, 2025 that produced nickel sized (0.88 inch) hail in San Simon, AZ. Additionally, heavy rainfall from thunderstorms caused flash flooding and closed Frontier Road in Cochise County.
episodes.207019: A nearly stationary thunderstorm on the afternoon of August 16th, 2025 caused flash flooding in the Tucson Metro. Water flooded the streets from curb to curb, roughly 6 inches of moving water, occurred in multiple locations. A nearby rain gauge reported 1.26 inches of rainfall fell in less than 1 hour.
episodes.207042: Several individual rounds of thunderstorms impacted western Wisconsin from Friday, August 16th through Sunday, August 18th. Heavy rain amounts on the order of 5-7 inches fell over the course of 72 hours, most of which fell from late Saturday into early Sunday, leading to at least one flooded roadway in Pepin County.
episodes.207184: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of Mississippi during the afternoon and evening hours of August 13th through 17th. Isolated damaging wind gusts occurred with the strongest of storms.
episodes.207189: Afternoon thunderstorms brought gusty winds and moderate rainfall to some of Lower Michigan. Isolated severe weather occurred.
episodes.207191: Major Hurricane Erin moved northeast and north of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Erin's Outer Bands and then Feeder Bands still affected the islands, producing strong thunderstorms, gusty winds, and heavy rains across the islands. Several reports of wind gust damage, along with reports of high surf, flooding and debris flow were received between August 16 to 18.
episodes.207200: Convective cloud lines developed along the Lower Florida Keys, with a report of a narrow waterspout received near Upper Sugarloaf Key.
episodes.207285: High pressure to the east and a trough to the west advected in a weak push of monsoon moisture, fueling isolated thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. A few produced severe weather and flooding.
episodes.208194: After a couple rounds of showers and thunderstorms through the day, a final round of disorganized convection during the late afternoon and evening crossing northern Michigan resulted in gusty winds near Lake Huron.

Power lines were blown down and sparking at IL-31 and Silver Glen Rd in St. Charles.
A tree was blown down at IL-47 and Beith Rd north of Elburn.
Corn was flattened near Main St just west of Bunker Rd southeast of Elburn.
Trees were downed onto wires and vehicles on Main St in Elburn.
A private weather station via Weather Underground reported rainfall of 3.25 inches  from around 5:45 pm EDT to 8 pm EDT.
Power poles were snapped in half at Harter Rd and County Line Rd south of Maple Park.
Trees and power lines were reported down along IL-47 between US-88 and Main St.
A 50-foot tree was uprooted in the vicinity of Green and Bunker roads west of Batavia. Damage to a corn field was also noted in the area.
Multiple little trees roughly 5 inches in diameter were snapped in half at the Spring Bluff nursery in Sugar Grove.

Based on information provided by Aurora emergency management, extensive storm damage was reported across Aurora with the Aurora Police and Streets Departments having collectively received well over 100 reports for tree and power line damage. The highest concentration of reports came out of the west side of town, particularly in the area bound by Prairie St and Indian Trail Rd to the south and north and Edgelawn Dr and Highland Ave to the west and east, respectively.
Multiple trees were down along Bliss Rd northeast of Sugar Grove.
Trees were down on houses and blocking roads near Tanner Rd and Terrace Dr near North Aurora.
A tree was down and blocking Winthrop New Rd in Prestbury.
Power lines were downed along Norris Rd in Sugar Grove.
Multiple trees were down along and blocking Seavey Rd in western Kane County.
A tree was down and blocking the road at Hankes Rd and Densmore Rd in western Aurora.
A tree was down and blocking Exposition Ave in North Aurora.
A tree and power lines were blown down on Rockwell Rd in Aurora.
A 12 inch diameter tree was snapped at its base and several 3 to 6 inch diameter tree limbs were down in the vicinity of IL-53 and Short St in Lisle.
Trees were downed onto power lines and vehicles near Prairie St and Edgelawn Dr in Aurora.
A tree roughly 12 to 14 feet tall and 2 to 3 feet thick fell onto a wire along Stephen Dr in Montgomery.
A healthy tree had split and was blocking a residential road in Aurora.
Multiple trees were blown down by severe thunderstorm wind gusts, with one tree landing  on a car. A nearby barn suffered the loss of its roof to the high storm winds.
Lightning struck a home along Hemingway Ct in Plainfield knocking out multiple electrical systems. Time was estimated based on radar data.

Roofing material was pulled off of a strip mall near IL-53 and Romeo Rd in Romeoville. A gas station canopy was also damaged and tilting nearby. Tree damage in the area extended from Romeoville High School north to Normantown Rd.

Multiple reports were received on social media for a funnel cloud in southern Will County. The most likely location based on the various reports appears to be over the Midewin Tallgrass Prairie in Wilmington.
Several large branches were broken in Lockport. The large trunk of a rotted tree also fell onto a house.
Whole trees were snapped in the vicinity of the Lockport High School baseball fields.
Drone footage and Sentinel satellite data showed circular damage to corn just west of the Vermilion County line and north of County Road 1100 North...consistent with a  microburst.
Sentinel satellite data showed a number of areas with corn damage south of the  intersection of Lincoln Trail Road and County Road 300 East.
Large tree limb fell onto a vehicle and is blocking the road. No injuries were reported.
Emergency management officials reported a large tree limb snapped and across the road. In addition, a tree adjacent to a road was uprooted, with some damage to the road.
A few 2-inch diameter tree limbs were blown down along North 130 East Road south of the Salt Fork.

Video and picture evidence showed a funnel cloud developing north of Homer.  Sentinel satellite data suggested a brief touchdown in a field about 1.5 miles east of the Champaign/Vermilion County line just north of Catlin-Homer Road.  Based on radar data, the tornado touched down at 6:47 PM CDT, then quickly lifted by 6:48 PM CDT.  No damage was reported.
Public report of nickel sized hail measured with a ruler.
Corn was blown down in a northeast to southwest direction just north of Catlin-Homer Road and west of North 130 East Road.

Video showed water from curb to curb and rushing with an estimated 6 inches of moving water along Mabel St from 2nd to 3rd Ave. A nearby rain gauge reported 1.26 inches of rainfall fell in less than 1 hour.
